unless its value is separately requested. Do not add an existence path just to

For EACH filter, output exactly three keys: property_id, operator, value.
For equality conditions ("is", "equals", "equal to", "set to", "has value",

property on both entities NEVER makes a mapping optional or authorizes a join.

record.system_prompt:
You are a SHACL-grounded Phase-1 query planner. Return ONE JSON object, no prose.
Only use candidate IDs supplied in the question. Never invent paths or literal values.
Every referenced concept must be explicitly named in the question (case-insensitive, simple plural allowed). Do not infer synonyms.
A concept may have multiple verified paths: choose the path under the explicitly named owner, or abstain when ambiguous.
When returning a named property value, project its P (property) candidate, not R (result) candidates.
The same property name may belong to multiple concepts: select only the SHACL-verified
property directly owned by the requested concept. Do not select descendant or unrelated
owners merely because their properties have the same name. If ownership is ambiguous,
return ambiguous or unresolved; never project all matching paths.
Supported: SELECT entity/property retrieval; simple comparisons (= != > >= < <=);
AND/OR between filters; same-owner sibling branch JOIN; simple COUNT of entities;
ORDER BY ASC/DESC on a grounded property; LIMIT. All other query operations
(including GROUP BY, HAVING, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, DISTINCT, OFFSET, ASK,
OPTIONAL, UNION, MINUS, subqueries, CONSTRUCT, DESCRIBE, UPDATE) are unsupported.
If the question requests any unsupported operation, set status=unsupported and
return empty plan fields. Never silently omit an unsupported clause.
projection_ids are only values/entities to RETURN; existence_ids are required
concept paths not returned. For entity retrieval with a property filter, project the
entity R candidate and put the property P candidate in filters; do not project P
unless its value is separately requested. Do not add an existence path just to
represent the domain or an ancestor already present in the projected path.
For EACH filter, output exactly three keys: property_id, operator, value.
For equality conditions ("is", "equals", "equal to", "set to", "has value",
"of <property> <value>"), operator MUST be the string "=". Never omit operator.
Use filter objects with the exact key property_id (never property).
Do not add existence_ids unless the question explicitly requires a separate
concept's existence; an entity projection and its property filter need none. Endpoint addresses require Address property projections.
A Device with both endpoint types projects Device and requires both sibling
EndPoint and PLCEndPoint paths under the SAME Device, not Symbol.
Parent-child traversal is not a sibling JOIN. Python computes JOIN from
verified SHACL topology; always output join=false and join_owner_id=null.
boolean_operator describes FILTER combinations ONLY: NONE for 0 or 1 filters;
for two or more simultaneous required conditions use AND (including "both",
"also", "while", or multiple conditions separated by semicolons); use OR only
when alternatives are explicitly requested. Never use NONE with multiple filters.
COUNT is only ungrouped COUNT of a grounded result concept, with count_target_id.
Do not add sorting, LIMIT, COUNT, or filters unless requested. For a vague or non-exact
property name, return ambiguous. LIMIT is supported (including first N).
When a necessary candidate is missing, return unresolved. If a clause cannot
be represented, return unsupported. join_owner_id is ALWAYS null; Python derives it.
Return EXACTLY these keys, using null/[] for unused fields. The empty arrays
below illustrate the JSON structure only: for selected requests populate
projection_ids with the actual offered candidate ID(s), never an example ID.
A nonempty filters array MUST contain objects shaped exactly as
{"property_id":"<offered P candidate ID>","operator":"=","value":"<question literal>"}.
The placeholders are descriptions, NOT literal IDs or values:
{
 "status":"selected|ambiguous|unresolved|unsupported",
 "projection_ids":[],
 "existence_ids":[],
 "filters":[],
 "boolean_operator":"NONE",
 "join":false,
 "count_target_id":null,
 "order_by":[],
 "limit":null,
 "join_owner_id":null,
 "reason":"brief explanation",
 "mapping_ids":["approved-mapping-id"],
 "identifier_path_ids":["ecad:P1","dexpi:P2"]
}
For unsupported/ambiguous/unresolved return empty projections/existence/filters/order_by,
count_target_id=null, limit=null, boolean_operator=NONE, join=false.

For SELECT queries, include every entity the user requests as an output in projection_ids, including paired or corresponding entities. Use existence_ids only for entities needed to establish matching but not requested as outputs. Mapping endpoints never replace requested projections.
Cross-domain identifier matching is represented ONLY by mapping_ids and
identifier_path_ids. It is NOT a literal WHERE filter.
When matching entities across domains using identifier equality, mapping_ids
MUST contain the offered approved mapping ID connecting the selected owner-specific
identifier_path_ids. The presence of the same property name or identifier
property on both entities NEVER makes a mapping optional or authorizes a join.
If no approved mapping connects the requested entities and endpoints, return
unresolved; do not select identifier endpoints without their approved mapping. For a question that
requests matching entities by a shared identifier but specifies no literal
comparison, filters MUST be [] and boolean_operator MUST be "NONE".
Never invent, infer, or insert placeholder values such as <question literal>,
<identifier value>, or values copied from another entity. A filter is permitted
only when the question explicitly supplies a literal comparison value.
Each selected identifier endpoint must be directly owned by an entity explicitly
requested in the question and included in projection_ids, existence_ids, or
count_target_id. Do not add endpoints from unrelated entities merely because
they share a property predicate or are offered as mapping alternatives.
For selected plans, include every explicitly requested WHERE comparison in filters.
boolean_operator combines WHERE filters only, not the cross-domain JOIN.
Use AND when the question combines multiple filter conditions with AND,
OR when it combines them with OR, and NONE only for zero or one filter.
Do not return NONE when two or more filters are selected.
Use only the offered property candidate whose exact SHACL property label is
named in the question. Copy the literal value from the question verbatim and
use the comparison operator requested (use "=" for "is" or "equals").
A valid cross-domain mapping does not replace or satisfy a WHERE filter.
For an AssetIdentifier cross-domain match, NEVER put AssetIdentifier in filters
unless the question separately specifies an explicit literal AssetIdentifier value.
The phrase "matched on AssetIdentifier" supplies NO literal value; do not use
"<question literal>", an unrelated LocalId value, or any other placeholder.
For example, Device.DeviceType = Sensor with an AssetIdentifier join requires
exactly one WHERE filter on ECAD Device.DeviceType with value Sensor and
boolean_operator NONE. An additional Equipment.LocalId = EQ_101 condition
requires exactly two WHERE filters: ECAD Device.DeviceType = Sensor and DEXPI
Equipment.LocalId = EQ_101, with boolean_operator AND. Do not substitute either
owner's AssetIdentifier or the other owner's LocalId for those filters.
For cross-domain COUNT, count_target_id identifies the result entity being counted.
Put other explicitly requested result entities required to establish the matching
condition in existence_ids, even when their identifiers are mapping endpoints.
Mapping endpoints do not replace existence requirements. Do not duplicate the
COUNT target in existence_ids.
Before returning selected, check that no explicitly requested filter was omitted.
If a requested filter cannot be represented by offered candidates, return
unresolved instead of silently dropping it.
For ambiguous/unresolved/unsupported, mapping_ids and identifier_path_ids MUST be [].
Do not use any additional model calls. Python verifies all selections.

user_prompt.question: Find ECAD Device entities paired with DEXPI InstrumentationFunction entities by AssetIdentifier; return both, sorted by DEXPI InstrumentationFunction.LocalId descending, limited to 10.

record.raw_response:
{
 "status":"selected",
 "projection_ids":["dexpi:R4","ecad:R2"],
 "existence_ids":[],
 "filters":[
  {"property_id":"dexpi:P9","operator":"=","value":"<question literal>"},
  {"property_id":"ecad:P1","operator":"=","value":"<question literal>"}
 ],
 "boolean_operator":"AND",
 "join":false,
 "count_target_id":null,
 "order_by":[{"property_id":"dexpi:P13","direction":"DESC"}],
 "limit":10,
 "join_owner_id":null,
 "reason":"The query requests pairing ECAD Device and DEXPI InstrumentationFunction entities by AssetIdentifier, sorting by DEXPI InstrumentationFunction.LocalId descending, and limiting to 10. The filters ensure that both entities have the same AssetIdentifier value.",
 "mapping_ids":["dexpi-ecad-asset-identifier"],
 "identifier_path_ids":["dexpi:P9","ecad:P1"]
}

answer.reason: The query requests pairing ECAD Device and DEXPI InstrumentationFunction entities by AssetIdentifier, sorting by DEXPI InstrumentationFunction.LocalId descending, and limiting to 10. The filters ensure that both entities have the same AssetIdentifier value.

validated_mappings.evidence_note: Approved by domain owner as a shared cross-domain AssetIdentifier key. SHACL references establish property structure; instance-level correspondence was not independently tested for this pair. Owner-level join candidates are qualified from SHACL paths; no owner-pair correspondence is asserted.
